newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PREMIER-DESIGNATE PRESENTS CABINET LINEUP.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PREMIER-DESIGNATE PRESENTS CABINET LINEUP.

text.p: Bulgaria's prime minister designate Ivan Kostov on Monday presented his proposed cabinet lineup to President Petar Stoyanov following his coalition's victory in April 19 elections.
The list, to be presented to parliament on Wednesday, names Muravei Radev, deputy chairman of the previous parliament's economic commission, as finance minister, Kostov told reporters.
Radev, 50, an economist by training, will implement reforms prescribed by the International Monetary Fund, including implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime.
Interim deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov retains the industry portfolio, with the task of restructuring the unwieldy state sector.
"We shall aim to restore confidence in Bulgaria and fulfil the pledges in the accord signed with the IMF, including introduction of a currency board system," Kostov said.

The new government's stated priorities are carrying out the IMF's reform programme, making provision for the social cost of reform, fighting organised crime, opening secret police files of public figures, returning land to its pre-communist owners, and bringing Bulgaria into the European Union and NATO.

"By July 30, we hope to adopt the most important laws for a currency board and economic stabilisation in order to meet the requirements of the international financial institutions and to be able to receive the second tranche from the IMF," Kostov said.

Nadezhda Mihailova, spokeswoman of Kostov's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), becomes foreign minister, and interim interior minister Bogomil Bonev will continue his high-profile campaign against organised crime and corruption.
Kostov will create a ministry of state administration to oversee reforms promised to reduce bureaucracy and improve the flow of information. The energy ministry will be downgraded to a committee.

The Financial Stabilisation Council advising the interim cabinet on Monday proposed the mark as anchor currency for the lev in the currency board, though the final decision must be made by Kostov's government and the new parliament, in which the UDF has a big majority.
The deputies, of whom 167 are in parliament for the first time, must also approve a 1997 budget.
